title: Hypothesis tests
overview: Set up null and alternative hypotheses, use a critical region or p-value, and draw a conclusion in the context of the question. This guide turns the current syllabus outcomes into a connected revision sequence: learn the ideas, practise the method, then use the recall cards and checklist to diagnose what still needs work.
syllabusPoints: State H₀ and H₁ and choose one- or two-tailed tests.
Use exact binomial/Poisson probabilities or suitable normal approximations.
Test a population mean with known variance or a large sample.
Calculate and interpret Type I and Type II error probabilities.

definitions.definition: H₀, the model or parameter value tested as the default claim.
H₁, the direction or difference supported if H₀ is rejected.
The maximum chosen probability of rejecting H₀ when it is true.
Test-statistic values that lead to rejection of H₀.
The probability under H₀ of an outcome at least as extreme as observed in the direction(s) of H₁.
Failing to reject a false H₀ under a specified alternative.

sections.title: Setting up the test
content: Define the parameter, write H₀ with equality, and make H₁ match the claim. 'Increased' gives an upper tail, 'decreased' a lower tail, and 'changed' two tails. The test calculation always uses the H₀ parameter.
bullets: Use population parameters, not sample statistics, in hypotheses.
Choose the tail before seeing the result.

sections.title: Discrete tests
content: For X binomial or Poisson, find the probability of the observed result or something more extreme under H₀. Reject if that p-value is ≤α. A critical region is chosen so its H₀ probability is at most α; discreteness means the actual size may be smaller.
bullets: For two tails, identify both extremes rather than blindly doubling if the distribution is asymmetric.
State the actual critical-region probability when requested.

sections.title: Normal and mean tests
content: Use a continuity-corrected normal approximation for binomial/Poisson when conditions hold. For a mean, standardise Z=(X̄−μ₀)/(σ/√n), using s for σ in a large-sample setting as allowed, then compare with the relevant critical value or p-value.
bullets: Put μ₀ from H₀ in the numerator.
A two-tailed α test places α/2 in each tail.

sections.title: Errors and conclusions
content: Type I probability is the rejection-region probability under H₀. Type II probability is the acceptance-region probability under a specified alternative. Finish with 'reject H₀' or 'do not reject H₀', followed by a contextual evidence statement—never say H₀ is proved.
bullets: The conclusion must use the direction in H₁.

examTips: Write hypotheses and significance level before calculating probabilities.
End with a decision and a separate sentence in the language of the question.
Show the mathematical setup and exact working before the final rounded answer; unsupported calculator output may not earn method marks.
commonMistakes: Using the observed sample proportion instead of the H₀ probability in a binomial test.
Forgetting α/2 in each tail of a two-tailed normal test.

quickRecall.question: Where does equality belong in hypotheses?
What tail matches 'the mean has decreased'?
What is a Type I error?
quickRecall.answer: Rejecting H₀ when H₀ is true.

quickRecall.question: How should a non-significant result be stated?
quickRecall.answer: Do not reject H₀; there is insufficient evidence for the contextual alternative claim.
